title: Nuevo Laredo deputy reports 13 initiatives approved and 1,300+ people served in second annual report
excerpt: State Deputy Gabriela Regalado Fuentes presented her second annual legislative report, with 13 initiatives approved in the last year and more than 1,300 people served through medical-assistance brigades in Nuevo Laredo.
content:
Gabriela Regalado Fuentes, the Morena state deputy for Nuevo Laredo's District 1, presented her second annual report on her legislative work, reporting 13 initiatives presented and approved and more than 1,300 people served through medical-assistance brigades and other support, according to Noticero.

The report was delivered in digital and printed form to Humberto Prieto Herrera, president of the governing board of the Tamaulipas Congress, as the law requires. Regalado said some of the 13 initiatives were focused on Nuevo Laredo's needs and others on strengthening the state's legal framework.

Among the topics she cited were proposals to increase penalties for the crime of femicide, and initiatives developed with the state Labor Department to update its legal provisions and give it new powers.

Beyond the chamber, Regalado said her district office in Nuevo Laredo has kept a presence on the ground, with medical-assistance brigades serving more than 1,300 people, plus medicines, orthopedic devices and support for medical transport for residents who needed care outside the city. The orthopedic-device program has run for about nine years.

Regalado said walking the neighborhoods lets her reconnect with people she has helped before — and that direct contact is one of the greatest satisfactions of the job.

Sources: Noticero (Jonathan Torres), Nov. 11, 2026.
